title: Private VPC bootstrap: resilient control-plane handshake and artifact sync acceptance
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood Private customers with strict VPC and air-gapped requirements currently report fragility during initial bootstrap and during image/artifact upgrade windows. The control-plane handshake (customer control plane connecting to Redwood control endpoints or relay proxies) and artifact synchronization (container images, signed manifests, operator snapshots) have multiple failure modes: intermittent egress blocking, expired signed manifests, and mis-ordered rollout steps that leave nodes in unrecoverable states.

Goal:
Define a minimal, testable contract and acceptance criteria for the bootstrap handshake and artifact sync flow that works across three network models: fully connected (egress allowed), egress-proxied (customer proxy/allowlist), and fully air-gapped (no outbound path). This ticket scopes the product requirements and acceptance tests; implementation will be split into ENG tickets for runtime, installer, and operator changes.

Out of scope:
- Full implementation of an on-prem artifact registry (ENG will use customer registries for now)
- Operator UI changes beyond status flags and short-lived diagnostics links

Key product decisions to capture here:
- Explicitly require a single 'bootstrap agent' handshake RPC (port and protocol defined) that can run over a designated proxy or direct egress; fallback behavior must be deterministic and documented.
- Signed manifest TTL must be configurable by customer; default safety window = 72 hours for upgrades and 14 days for initial bootstrap artifacts.
- When in air-gapped mode, an offline artifact validation path is required: a locally-provided signed bundle + checksum manifest that the agent can validate without external reachability.
- Rollout semantics: if >10% of pool nodes fail manifest validation during an upgrade, abort and auto-rollback to last known-good model image.

Non-functional constraints:
- End-to-end bootstrap should complete in <20 minutes for networks with only a 500 Mbps initial sync link (benchmark for large customers).
- Diagnostic logs and a one-click support bundle must be producible from the console for at least the last 6 hours of bootstrap events.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Anya Patel (owner)
- ENG lead: Marcus Reed
- Security: Chen Wang
- Solutions/SE: Priya Narang
acceptance_criteria: Handshake contract: The product doc lists exact TCP/UDP ports, TLS requirements, and proxy header requirements. Test harness proves successful handshake via direct, proxied, and offline-bundle modes.
Artifact sync modes: The installer supports three artifact acquisition modes (egress, proxy-with-allowlist, offline-bundle) and each mode has a documented validation path and error codes.
Manifest TTL behavior: Default TTLs apply and are configurable via installer flags; tests simulate expired manifests and show safe abort/rollback behavior.

Rollback guardrail: During a staged upgrade (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%), if >10% of nodes fail validation at any stage, the control plane aborts and rolls back automatically; a test run demonstrates this with injected failures.

Air-gapped validation: Operator can provide a signed bundle (local tarball + checksum + signature) that the bootstrap agent validates without outbound access; acceptance test runs without internet connectivity.

Observability: Console exposes per-node bootstrap status, last-successful-manifest-id, and a link to a downloadable 6-hour support bundle; test includes verifying bundle contents contain logs, manifest.json, and network traces.
Performance: Full bootstrap (including downloading 10GB of artifacts over a 500 Mbps link) completes within 20 minutes in our lab benchmark; SLO verification artifacts attached to ticket.
Security: All control-plane handshakes use mTLS; configuration allows customer KMS-backed verification of signer keys. Security review (attached) signed off.
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting with ENG, Security, and SE. Captured initial failure modes from three customers (Customer A,B,C). See notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PRV-boot-2025-01-12

2025-01-20: Design review — ENG proposed adding a deterministic proxy header handshake that requires proxy to forward X-Forwarded-For and TLS passthrough. Security flagged replay concerns; ENG accepted signed nonce approach. (Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/priv-bootstrap-design)
2025-01-28: Scope change approved: include configurable manifest TTLs and a test harness for expired-manifest injection. Tracked as dependency ENG-5890.
2025-02-03: Draft acceptance criteria posted; SE requested explicit support-bundle contents and per-node debug artifacts. Added to acceptance criteria list.

2025-02-08: Security review scheduled; Chen Wang provided initial signoff on mTLS + KMS signer model but requested proof-of-concept for offline bundle signature verification (see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-installer/pull/214).
qa_plan: Create three lab topologies: direct-egress, egress-with-proxy (allowlist), fully-airgapped (no external connectivity).
Automate bootstrap runs nightly against each topology; collect metrics into QA dashboard and record failures with trace IDs.
Create fuzz tests to corrupt manifests and validate rollback semantics work as expected.
Run performance benchmark: 10GB artifact sync over throttled 500 Mbps link and record time-to-ready.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: increasing default manifest TTL reduces churn for customers but increases window for revoked signatures — proposed compromise: short default for upgrades (72h) and longer for initial bootstrap (14d) with customer override.
Open question: Should we support delta/patch diffs for artifact sync to reduce egress? Engineering to evaluate delta patch complexity (ENG-4123).
Follow-up: Create ENG tasks for operator status flags, support-bundle generator, and offline-bundle signature verification PoC.
